title: Sycophancy Stress Test: Emotional Pressure vs. Logical Pressure vs. Authority Pressure

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Comparing pressure types across model families reveals which resistance profiles exist and which models are vulnerable to which attacks. Useful for auditors but somewhat descriptive rather than mechanistic.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Three matched pressure conditions tested via API across 4 models is straightforward. No model training needed. Prompt engineering and result analysis are well within beginner capability. API costs for 4 models are moderate.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Clear deliverable: capitulation rate comparison across 3 pressure types and 4 model families. Well-defined factorial design with clear output. 30 hours is feasible, especially if questions are shared across conditions.

novelty.reasoning: The comparison of pressure types for sycophancy has been directly studied. (1) SycEval-EM (arXiv:2601.16529, 2026) compares five persuasion tactics (including emotional, authority, citation pressure) in clinical settings, finding comparable effectiveness at 30-36% acquiescence with Citation Pressure marginally highest at 36%. Emotional Fear was highest in specific scenarios (44%). (2) 'When Truth Is Overridden' (arXiv:2508.02087) shows opinion-driven mechanisms dominate authority-driven ones. (3) Northeastern News (Feb 2026) reports on context and role effects on sycophancy. (4) 'How Can You Avoid LLM Sycophancy? Keep it Professional' (2026) provides practical findings. The three-way comparison proposed here (emotional vs logical vs authority) is substantially covered by existing stress testing across model families.
